Q: Difference between math.exp(2) and math.e**2 A:

It's different due to differences in the implementation of the functions. Neither one is perfect due to the nature of floating point.

The ** operator is implemented in floatobject.c and contains a lot of special cases, but none of them are invoked here, so it ultimately reaches the standard C pow function. The math.pow function ultimately does the same thing.

The exp function is a straightforward wrapper around the C function of the same name, defined with a macro in mathmodule.c.

As it happens, exp is more precise (both of the results match, to within the precision allowed by floating point, high-precision answers I calculated in bc). Most likely it is because internally to pow, it is calculating the extended-precision logarithm of the double-precision e value you pass as the first argument, which is slightly smaller than 1.

The fundamental issue is that math.e, which is the number you're calculating the power of, is:

2.718281828459045 09079559829...

Whereas the real value of e is

2.718281828459045 23536028747...

And this error is compounded when you use pow or **, whereas it may not be (or may be using a higher precision value internally) if you're using exp due to the details of the algorithms it uses.

Q: Why does my Pod stay in ImagePullBackOff after I just ran docker build locally, when the exact same tag exists in my local Docker daemon? A:

This is a common misconception. Simply put, your host Docker daemon and the k3d cluster do not share an image store.

Your command - docker build -t myapp:dev . - puts the image in the host Docker daemon. k3d runs Kubernetes nodes as containers, and those nodes use their own containerd image stores. So, the kubelet asks the node’s container runtime for myapp:dev and that runtime does not have it. Hence, so Kubernetes treats the unqualified name as docker.io/library/myapp:dev and tries Docker Hub.

What you can do is import the image into k3d, then import it. After that, restart your deployment.

k3d cluster list  
k3d image import myapp:dev --cluster \<cluster-name\>  
kubectl rollout restart deployment/myapp  
kubectl rollout status deployment/myapp

Ideally, you would want to set up a local registry. You can read more on that here.

Q: Java Stream - what is the difference between filter() and dropWhile() A:

filter() checks every element and keeps all elements that match the predicate.

dropWhile() removes elements only from the beginning of the stream while the predicate is true. Once it encounters the first element for which the predicate is false, it keeps that element and all subsequent elements.

List<Integer> numbers = List.of(1, 2, 3, 1, 4);

numbers.stream()
    .filter(n -> n < 3)
// [1, 2, 1]

numbers.stream()
    .dropWhile(n -> n < 3)
// [3, 1, 4]

In short:

  • filter(predicate) → keeps every element matching the predicate.

  • dropWhile(predicate) → removes only the matching prefix of the stream.
